review_evidence: AWS PutTargets can attach a Lambda target to an exact rule, and Lambda must authorize events.amazonaws.com for that rule. PutEvents can supply a matching event, but invoking fixed code does not automatically expose its execution role. A definite principal edge needs the same rule and bus, both source grants, exact Lambda resource policy, accepted event pattern and a handler behavior that lets the source drive role-authorized actions or obtain credentials. Current collector has no such handler-input witness; AWS PutTargets, PutEvents and Lambda resource-policy docs.

PutPermission can change an event-bus policy so a controlled principal can publish, which may be a bounded self-permission gain even without another IAM role. Confirm the exact principal and bus, accepted policy statement, effective PutEvents permission before and after, and explicit denies; any downstream role edge additionally needs a matching rule, authorized target and behavior controlled through event input. AWS PutPermission and event-bus policy docs.

AWS PutRule can enable a disabled rule while its targets remain attached, but the request replaces omitted rule fields and may break the rule. A role edge needs the exact disabled rule, a complete valid schedule or pattern that will fire, an already authorized target, and target behavior that exercises role authority for the source. PutRule on a rule alone proves only the control-plane change; AWS PutRule and PutTargets docs.

AWS StartReplay re-emits an archive's retained events into its bus; it cannot edit the event payload, rule or target. A role edge needs an exact archive/bus, effective StartReplay on required resources, a retained event in the selected interval, a still matching rule and an authorized target whose fixed behavior yields additional principal authority. Current inventory does not join archive contents to the target effect; AWS StartReplay and archive docs.

This existing-API route changes the role and IAM-signed HTTP endpoint on a data source, unlike the active new-API CreateDataSource route and unlike UpdateResolver reuse of an existing role. AWS UpdateResolver can repoint a field, but a definite role edge also needs one exact callable API field, effective UpdateDataSource and UpdateResolver grants, PassRole with appsync.amazonaws.com, AppSync trust and an invocation authorization path. Current collector has only API summaries, so it cannot join those facts. AWS CreateDataSource, UpdateResolver, HTTP resolver and AppSync authorization docs.

exclusion_technique: Replace an existing AppStream fleet image or session-script archive while retaining its role
review_evidence: AWS UpdateFleet permits ImageArn on a RUNNING Always-On or On-Demand fleet while keeping its existing IamRoleArn; new instances use the new image. The active PassRole UpdateFleet route changes the role, so it does not cover image substitution. A definite principal edge needs one exact fleet and role, source UpdateFleet on that fleet and any required image resource, an image the source can control and the fleet can use, and a future instance/session execution path. The current inventory has fleet-role details but does not prove image ownership or control. AWS UpdateFleet API and Update a Fleet with a New Image guide.

exclusion_technique: Create a container fleet with a passed role and controlled container group
review_evidence: AWS CreateContainerFleet requires FleetRoleArn and a named container group definition to deploy containers. The active CreateBuild plus CreateFleet route does not authorize this separate API. A definite role path needs exact group definition/image ownership, source CreateContainerGroupDefinition and CreateContainerFleet permissions, PassRole to GameLift, deployment and role credential availability in a controlled container. Current collector does not join those facts; AWS CreateContainerFleet API.

exclusion_technique: Create an EC2 fleet with a passed role and a pre-existing controlled build or script
review_evidence: A source may choose an existing game build or script in CreateFleet without CreateBuild, but its control of that exact executable and a runnable startup path are not established by the fleet and PassRole grants. The active route covers a newly created/uploadable build only. Need exact artifact-control, fleet request and role joins before a separate edge; AWS CreateFleet and CreateBuild APIs.

exclusion_technique: Replace an EMR Serverless application's custom image for future workloads
review_evidence: AWS documents that UpdateApplication can change imageConfiguration for some running applications and later workloads use the new image. This does not imply existing jobs change or a role session begins. A principal edge needs exact application permission, a controlled compatible ECR image, service pull access, digest-resolution and capacity state, a later workload using that image, its execution role and an executable image component. Current collector does not join these facts; AWS Updating Running Applications and Customizing an EMR Serverless Image docs.

exclusion_technique: Remove an SCP guardrail for a controlled member principal
review_evidence: An SCP change can unlock a member principal only when its existing identity policy allows the exact action and this was the effective block. The management caller is not restricted by that SCP. Need a controlled member principal, exact account/policy inheritance, effective action before and after, and no other deny or boundary. AWS SCP guide and Organizations delegation-policy supported actions.

exclusion_technique: Delegate Organizations policy actions to a controlled member principal
review_evidence: PutResourcePolicy can delegate supported policy actions to a member account, but it must be accepted for the exact actions/resources and a controlled member principal must also hold matching identity permission without blocking guardrails. The management writer does not automatically obtain a new principal edge. Current inventory lacks the controlled-member and before/after authorization join; AWS Organizations resource-based delegation policy docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach an existing useful Automation document to automatic Config remediation
review_evidence: An existing Automation document can remove the CreateDocument permission requirement from the active route. The source still needs exact PutRemediationConfigurations and PassRole to SSM, an eligible non-service-linked rule with a noncompliant resource, automatic mode and service-linked role, plus a document step accepted under the passed role that yields additional authority. Current collector does not establish the document content and same-rule execution join; AWS Config PutRemediationConfigurations and remediation docs.

exclusion_technique: Create and open a legacy EMR notebook on a privileged cluster
review_evidence: AWS disabled new notebook creation in the old console. The notebook service role supports network and storage, while code runs on the attached cluster. Restore a principal route only if the legacy API is supported and exact READY editor, source kernel access, cluster role, runtime isolation and workload effect are joined; AWS EMR notebook migration and service-role documentation.

exclusion_technique: Open an existing legacy EMR editor attached to a privileged cluster
review_evidence: OpenEditorInConsole does not itself vend IAM credentials. A definite route needs a supported READY editor and cluster, caller access to run a notebook cell, exact cluster instance or runtime role and accepted workload; current collector has no editor-to-cluster-to-role join. AWS EMR notebook migration, service-role and runtime-role documentation.
